prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1451; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured after a collision at an intersection while turning left. The insured is named on the policy and the claimant is represented by counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Police attended and confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle that was struck. Photos from the scene and statements from two independent witnesses match the insured's account of how the collision happened, and the other driver has confirmed it as well.

Entry 3: Vehicle damage is consistent with the described impact and the wrist fracture reported by the claimant's medical provider fits the force expected from this type of crash. Prior medical records show a minor strain in the same area years ago that healed fully.

Entry 4: A neighbor has told our field representative they believe the vehicle was already damaged a few weeks before the claimed loss. No prior damage to the vehicle is recorded in our files, and we are following up to verify this statement.

Entry 5: The claimant has added some smaller details to the account since first reporting, but the core description of the collision has not changed. Treatment has followed a usual course and the claimant's reported symptoms have tapered as recovery progressed.

Entry 6: File remains open pending review of the neighbor's statement and receipt of the remaining medical records from counsel. The overall picture is being assessed against the physical evidence and the timeline of treatment.
